Soft-thresholded ridge (STR) estimator

Source: R/hr.R
hr.Rd

Fits the soft-thresholded ridge estimator \(\hat\theta_j = sign(\hat\beta_{k,j})(|\hat\beta_{k,j}| - \gamma)_+\), where \(\hat\beta_k\) is the ridge estimator with ridge parameter k. The estimator has an explicit form and is valid for \(p > n\).

Usage

hr(
  X,
  y,
  k,
  gamma,
  intercept = TRUE,
  standardize = TRUE,
  nonneg = FALSE,
  scale = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'hr'
coef(object, ik = 1, ig = 1, ...)

# S3 method for class 'hr'
predict(object, newx, ik = 1, ig = 1, ...)

Arguments

X

n x p design matrix.

y

response vector of length n.

k

ridge parameter(s), positive.

gamma

threshold(s), nonnegative. Thresholds apply on the scale of the standardized design when standardize = TRUE.

intercept

logical, fit an unpenalized intercept by centring.

standardize

logical, scale columns of X to unit variance.

nonneg

logical, use the nonnegative variant \((\hat\beta_{k,j} - \gamma)_+\).

scale

For hr, logical training least-squares rescaling (SSTR-LS). For hr_risk, a fixed positive numeric scale; not a random fitted scale.

object

a fitted "hr" object.

ik, ig

indices of the ridge parameter and threshold to use.

...

unused.

newx

matrix of new predictor values.

Value

An object of class "hr" containing the coefficient array beta of dimension p x length(k) x length(gamma) on the original scale, the intercepts a0, and the tuning grids.

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(50 * 200), 50, 200)
y <- X[, 1:3] %*% c(3, -2, 1.5) + rnorm(50)
fit <- hr(X, y, k = 10, gamma = 0.1)
which(coef(fit)[-1] != 0)
#>  [1]   1   2   3  10  11  18  19  22  25  26  27  28  37  39  44  47  49  52  55
#> [20]  60  65  66  68  73  78  81  88  90  92  96  97  98 100 101 102 105 113 115
#> [39] 119 121 122 126 128 130 132 134 136 138 140 144 148 149 151 162 163 164 165
#> [58] 167 172 174 175 176 181 182 185 191 192 193 197 199 200
